summary: The tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62) in the Valley of the Kings was found almost intact by Howard Carter in 1922. It held more than five thousand objects, many of them gold, now shown together at the Grand Egyptian Museum near the Giza pyramids.
facts: Howard Carter found the first step of the tomb on 4 November 1922, in the Valley of the Kings. His sponsor was Lord Carnarvon.
On 26 November 1922 Carter looked through a small hole into the tomb by candlelight. Asked if he could see anything, he answered, as he later wrote, "Yes, wonderful things."
The tomb held more than five thousand objects. Clearing and recording them took Carter about ten years.
Tutankhamun became king as a boy of about eight or nine, ruled for about nine or ten years, and died at about nineteen, around 1323 BC.
His burial mask is made of about ten kilograms of gold, inlaid with lapis lazuli, quartz, obsidian and coloured glass.
The king lay in three coffins, one inside the other. The innermost coffin is solid gold and weighs about 110 kilograms.
Four gilded wooden shrines stood one inside the other around his stone sarcophagus.
One of the daggers buried with him has an iron blade. A study published in 2016 found that the iron came from a meteorite.
His golden throne shows the young king and his queen Ankhesenamun.
Six chariots were found in the tomb.
The tomb was entered by robbers twice in ancient times, soon after the burial, and was sealed again.
The tomb is small for a king, and some historians believe it was not first made for him.
Lord Carnarvon died in Cairo in April 1923 after an infected mosquito bite, which started the story of a curse.
common_myths: There is no evidence of a real curse: most of the people who entered the tomb lived for many years afterwards.
